title: Final Comprehensive Assessment
description: This quiz covers all conditions from all modules.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of ulnar sided thumb pain?
questions.explanation: UCL dysfunction is the most common cause of ulnar sided thumb pain.

questions.question: Which special test is positive in De Quervain's tenosynovitis?
questions.explanation: The Finkelstein test is positive in De Quervain's tenosynovitis.

questions.question: A Colle's fracture results from a FOOSH on which wrist position?
questions.explanation: Colle's fracture occurs from a FOOSH on an extended wrist, causing dorsal displacement ("dinner fork" appearance).

questions.question: Why should extrinsic hand muscle strengthening be avoided in RA patients?
options: It increases ulnar drift due to ulnar-sided forces
Extrinsic muscles are not affected in RA
questions.explanation: Activation of extrinsic hand muscles increases ulnar drift due to the ulnar-sided forces of the extrinsic hand muscles. Only intrinsic hand muscle strengthening should be given.

questions.question: In FPL tenosynovitis, AROM is more provocative than RROM because:
options: Active movement requires more muscle force
The tendon moves through the irritated sheath during active movement
Passive structures are more stressed during AROM
questions.explanation: With tenosynovitis, irritation is between the tendon and the sheath. AROM causes the tendon to be pulled through the sheath, creating friction.

questions.question: Dupuytren contracture primarily affects which tissue?
questions.explanation: Dupuytren contracture is an overproduction of fibrous tissue within the palmar fascia. It does not involve muscle, tendons, or neuromuscular dysfunction.

questions.question: Which two special tests are positive in TFCC injury?
options: UCL stress test and grind test
Ulnocarpal stress test and ulnar impaction test
questions.explanation: The ulnocarpal stress test and ulnar impaction test are positive in TFCC injury.

questions.question: Morning stiffness lasting over 2 hours is more characteristic of osteoarthritis than rheumatoid arthritis.
questions.explanation: RA usually has morning stiffness over 2 hours. OA usually has morning stiffness under 1 hour.

questions.question: If thumb pain is recreated during radial deviation of the wrist, which condition is most likely?
questions.explanation: CMC 1 OA is the most likely condition if thumb pain is recreated during radial deviation, because radial deviation is a compressive force on the CMC 1.

questions.question: What structure does trigger finger surgery address?
questions.explanation: Surgery addresses the A1 pulley (not the tendon or nodule).

questions.question: Significant edema is a common finding in isolated TFCC injuries.
questions.explanation: Edema following TFCC injury is rare and normally only occurs with combined injuries such as fracture.

questions.question: Which nodes are found at the PIP joints in osteoarthritis?
questions.explanation: Bouchard's nodes are found at the PIPs. Heberden's nodes are found at the DIPs.

questions.question: What should always be ruled out following a FOOSH injury before treating as a wrist sprain?
questions.explanation: FOOSH injuries commonly cause fractures and/or dislocations, so these should always be ruled out.

questions.question: Why is the scaphoid fracture of particular clinical concern?
options: It is susceptible to avascular necrosis
It causes immediate carpal tunnel syndrome
It is the most painful fracture type
questions.explanation: The scaphoid is susceptible to avascular necrosis following fracture, which can lead to SLAC wrist arthritis.

questions.question: Which muscle provides the most helpful muscular support for a healing UCL of MCP 1?
questions.explanation: The 1st dorsal interossei manus muscle is the most helpful muscular support for the healing UCL ligament.
